properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 is shipped as a hashing option in the crypto layer of every language port (cs `SHA1.Create()`/`SHA1CryptoServiceProvider`, java Crypto/BaseExchange, js `legacy_js.sha1`, vendored noble-hashes sha1 in the published cjs bundle, mirrored in test bridges). Reachable via the hash()/hmac() algorithm dispatch when an exchange requires it. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 is a hash dispatch option in each port's crypto layer (cs `MD5.Create()`/`MD5CryptoServiceProvider`, java Crypto, vendored noble-hashes md5 in the published cjs bundle). Classically broken hash retained as API surface for exchanges that require it. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The same throwaway RSA keypair PEM is embedded as a fixture in each port's generated cryptography unit tests (cs/tests, go/tests, java/tests, js/src/test, php/test, ...). It is committed hardcoded private-key material, but test-only: used to exercise the rsa() signing method, never loaded at runtime. Changeable here (rotate fixture to a generated key if desired).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-MD5 is implemented and dispatched in the C# crypto layer (SignHMACMD5, chosen via the hmac() algorithm registry at Exchange.Crypto.cs:72), with equivalents in the go port, plus the vendored crypto-js HmacMD5 helper inlined in the published cjs bundle. Shipped MAC surface; classically weak. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RC4/RC4Drop ship inside the vendored crypto-js library that the bundler inlines wholesale into dist/cjs output (the published artifact carries the algorithms); jsencrypt's jsbn prng4 uses an Arcfour PRNG internally for RSA keygen seeding. No application call site invokes RC4 for data. Presence is the inventory question here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TripleDES ships inside the vendored crypto-js library inlined into the published cjs bundle (dist build output). No application call site encrypts data with 3DES; the artifact carries the algorithm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 in two roles: (1) live — EVM wallet signing in every port's ethMethods (EIP-191/EIP-712 ECDSA), backed by the vendored Cryptography.ECDSA Secp256k1Manager (cs), noble-curves/elliptic secp256k1 (js/dist), k256 (rust examples); (2) references — build-transpiler algorithm-name tables describing the same surface. Shor-vulnerable ECDSA over live wallet private keys; migration to ML-DSA/PQ wallet schemes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Generated multi-port test fixtures: placeholder API secrets ("secretsecretsecret..."), test EC private keys for ethMethods/ecdsa tests, and dummy exchange.privateKey values across cs/tests/Generated and the equivalent generated tests in other ports. Committed hardcoded secret-shaped strings, but test-only placeholders — not live credentials. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: System.Random/Math.random used for non-security purposes: request-ID/jitter generation in the cs and js ports (Exchange.cs, dist Exchange.js), test race conditions, and crypto-js's internal word-array seeding. Exchange API nonces in ccxt are timestamp-based, so no signature/keygen context found. Weak PRNG presence (CWE-338 class) but not crypto-reachable from the sampled sites. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HitBTC WebSocket (pro) authentication JWTs are signed HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) in every port (cs/go/java/js, plus dist build output); java base Crypto.java maps the JWT alg names HS256/384/512 onto JCA HmacSHA256/384/512. HMAC-SHA256 is the exchange-mandated auth scheme. Changeable here only by the exchange.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA private-key loading and SIGNING in the cs port's crypto layer (DecodeRSAPrivateKey, RSACryptoServiceProvider.ImportParameters, SignData) and the java equivalent, used for exchanges whose API auth requires RSA-signed (RS256) requests; the vendored NodeRSA library is inlined into the published js bundle. This is RSA signing (Shor → ML-DSA path), distinct from any RSA encryption.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA-PSS request SIGNING in four ports (cs SignData+RSASignaturePadding.Pss, go rsa.SignPSS with PSSSaltLengthEqualsHash, java Signature RSASSA-PSS, python padding.PSS/MGF1) — the PSS variant some exchanges require for signed requests. RSA signature → ML-DSA/SLH-DSA migration.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (at least Node.js 18.0.0)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Node 18+ default TLS: TLS 1.3 with X25519 ECDHE key exchange — quantum-vulnerable (harvest-now-decrypt-later) against passively captured traffic. Example proxy-usage script; default settings because nothing configures groups. Changeable here (Node supports hybrid X25519MLKEM768 via --tls-default-groups or defaultKeyChain? via NODE options).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Rust port ships an HMAC-SHA-1 arm in its hmac dispatch (exchange.rs match on "sha1" → HmacSha1) — live MAC surface; plus the vendored crypto-js HmacSHA1 helper inlined in the published cjs bundle. HMAC-SHA1 is quantum-relevant only via Grover; classically 160-bit truncated MACs are acceptable, but the surface ships. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the python port's rsa() request-SIGNER: it builds a JWT-style payload and signs with RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 (padding.PKCS1v15, SHA-256). The site is real crypto, but the operation is RSA signing, not encryption — migration target ML-DSA/SLH-DSA, not ML-KEM.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile-declared ECDSA-over-secp256k1 dependency in the rust examples workspace (k256/ecdsa crates in examples/rust/Cargo.lock) — dependency inventory: the built example binaries link secp256k1 ECDSA. Reachable from examples only, not the rust ccxt library itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: secp256k1 library (@noble/curves or equivalent) declared in docs/playground/package-lock.json — the docs playground app links secp256k1 support. The main library's live secp256k1 usage is inventoried under the secp256k1 object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP-0039 mnemonic-to-seed derivation, vendored scure-bip39 in the published cjs bundle: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with c=2048, dkLen=64 — the iteration count is fixed by the BIP39 specification for mnemonic derivation (not a password verifier, so the OWASP password minimum does not apply; it is still a KDF a quantum adversary speeds up only quadratically).

components.name: Java JSSE sessions on default settings (at least JDK 21)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Java port's HTTP client (BaseExchange) rides JSSE defaults — JDK 21 offers TLS 1.3 X25519 ECDHE, no PQ KEX. This is the shipped library's transport for all exchange API traffic; harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure. Changeable here only by explicit SSLParameters with hybrid groups (JDK 21 does not yet enable them by default).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 across the target: live signing for Kraken (ed25519 API keys) and Coinbase EdDSA JWTs in every port's crypto layer (cs BouncyCastle Ed25519PrivateKeyParameters, go ed25519, js noble/tweetnacl, rust ed25519-dalek), plus build-transpiler name tables and docs baselines referencing it. Shor-vulnerable signature path on live exchange credentials; migration ML-DSA.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA across the target, with the Stark-curve variant now read: the cs port's base Exchange.retrieveStarkAccount (Exchange.cs:1007-1008) drives StarkSharp's ECDSA over the custom Stark curve (field prime 2^251+17·2^192+1, Pedersen-hash message encoding, Poseidon-based address computation) — live for the Paradex exchange implementation (paradex.cs:1821). Live standard-curve ECDSA: Coinbase ES256 JWTs (cs ECDsa/nistP256 + equivalents in all ports), EVM wallet signing over secp256k1 in ethMethods.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256/secp256r1 in two roles: (1) live — the cs port signs Coinbase ES256 JWTs with ECCurve.NamedCurves.nistP256 (Exchange.Crypto.cs:691) and equivalents in other ports; (2) vendored — Portable.BouncyCastle's NIST/SEC curve registries shipped in the cs port. Shor-vulnerable ECDSA on live credentials.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Coinbase (Advanced/International) API authentication JWTs signed ES256 — ECDSA over P-256/secp256r1 with SHA-256 — in every port (cs ECDsa with ECCurve.NamedCurves.nistP256, js jwt(), go, java, php async, python, dist build output). Shor-vulnerable signatures on live trading credentials. Changeable here only when Coinbase offers a PQ JWT alg.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Coinbase API authentication JWTs signed EdDSA (Ed25519) in every port (cs, js, go, java, php async, dist). Shor-vulnerable signature path for live trading credentials; the seed private key is the API secret. Migration: ML-DSA when the exchange supports it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored library surface only: X25519 OIDs in the vendored Portable.BouncyCastle (cs), Curve25519 curve definitions in vendored elliptic-php (php static dep) and noble-curves/elliptic (dist bundle). The libraries ship X25519/Curve25519 support; no application key-agreement call site exists in ccxt. Presence is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: ed25519 libraries declared in docs/playground/package-lock.json and the rust examples workspace (ed25519-dalek and friends in examples/rust/Cargo.lock). The playground and example binaries link Ed25519 signature support; the main library's Ed25519 use is inventoried separately under the Ed25519 object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: A PKCS#8 private key is committed inside the revolutx request/response test fixtures (content-identified by its bytes). Test-only credential material for the Revolut exchange implementation tests — committed key material, not a live credential. Changeable here (regenerate fixtures).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (SHA-3 family) in every port: ethChecksumAddress (EIP-55 address checksums), solidityKeccak/keccak256 in the EVM helper methods, keccakMessage wrappers, plus build-transpiler algorithm-name tables and generated mirrors. Not a NIST-SHA3 deployment — EVM-required Keccak. Quantum-relevant only via Grover. Changeable only by the EVM protocol.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The primary request-signing primitive of the entire library: HMAC-SHA256/384/512 implemented in every port's crypto layer (cs SignHMACSHA256/384/512, java, go, python hmac, php hash_hmac, rust Hmac crates) and invoked by nearly every exchange implementation for API authentication. Also vendored crypto-js/noble-hashes HMAC in the js bundle. HMAC with SHA-2 is quantum-degraded only via Grover; it is the exchange-mandated scheme (changeable only by each exchange).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in every port's crypto layer (cs SHA256.Create, java MessageDigest SHA-256, python hashlib, php hash, go, rust) — used for exchange signatures, JWT payloads, and hashing helpers; also inside the vendored StarkSharp Poseidon implementation. Quantum-relevant only via Grover.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored PBKDF2 implementations (crypto-js PBKDF2, noble-hashes pbkdf2) inlined into the published cjs bundle; the only live use is scure-bip39's BIP39 mnemonic derivation (inventoried separately as PBKDF2-low-iterations). Library-surface presence in the shipped artifact.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-384/SHA-512 across all ports, both as hash wrappers and as HMAC inputs for exchange auth (bit2c, bitbns, bitfinex HMAC-SHA384/512 signatures, etc.). Part of the exchange-mandated signing surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: SHAKE256 XOF via golang.org/x/crypto/sha3 declared in examples/benchmarks/go/go.mod — benchmark binaries link SHAKE256.

properties.name: pqs:context

These are CSPRNGs (positive control: key generation uses secure randomness); part of the shipped library surface.
